I added a `habit remind` command. It lists the habits you haven't marked done today, and if a habit has a streak running through yesterday, it tells you so you don't break it:

```
$ habit remind
Not done yet today (2026-09-27):
- read
- run (keep your 4-day streak going)
```

If every habit is done it prints `All habits done for 2026-09-27. Nice!`, and with no habits it shows the usual "add one" hint. All 11 tests pass, including 4 new ones for `remind`.

**Changes:**
- `src/commands.js`: new `remind()` function. It takes an optional date so it can be tested.
- `src/cli.js`: added the `remind` command and updated the usage line.
- `src/streak.js`: made the one-day constant (`DAY`) available to other files.
- `test/commands.test.js`: tests for pending habits, a streak at risk, all done, and no habits.
- `README.md`: added the command to the examples.

**Things to know:**
- **It only runs when you call it.** The reminder isn't sent on a schedule. To get nudged automatically, run `habit remind` from your shell startup file or a cron job; the README says this too.
- **"Today" means the UTC date, not your local date.** That's how the app already records days. Depending on your time zone, the reminder can switch to a new day in the evening or the morning.
- **One edit was blocked.** My first attempt to write the changes with a single Python script was refused because it needed permission, which this session can't grant. I made the same changes with the file editing tools instead, so nothing is missing.

I haven't committed anything.
